title: PUT /api/orders/ship lets any authenticated user mark any order shipped - no admin/role enforcement
owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: Ordering.API/
out_of_scope_hunks: tests/Ordering.FunctionalTests/OrderingApiTests.cs (three test hunks, forced by the fix)
rationale: Registers a named 'admin' policy (RequireAuthenticatedUser + RequireRole) in Program.cs and chains .RequireAuthorization("admin") onto only the /ship mapping. FAIL-CLOSED by design: no token in the solution currently carries an admin role claim (Identity.API's ProfileService emits no role claim; Ordering.API has no role store), so every ship request is 403 until an operator maps real admins. /cancel deliberately untouched (separate finding).
variants_checked: Only two RequireAuthorization sites repo-wide; no policies or role checks existed before; all seven route mappings reviewed; /cancel deferred per finding scope.
bypass_considered: Non-admin JWT + any OrderNumber now dies in authorization middleware with 403 before the handler; only a deliberately minted admin-claim token ships orders (the intended grant path).
test_note: ShipOrderRequiresAdminRole asserts 403 for an authenticated non-admin in tests/Ordering.FunctionalTests/OrderingApiTests.cs; two pre-existing ship tests updated to expect Forbidden.
review_reason: Endpoint-level policy is the correct layer (the handler has no principal access); verified fail-closed since no issuer emits role claims; test changes are forced consequences, not scope creep.
